name: Authelia
abstract: Authelia is a community-driven, open-source (Apache 2.0) 2FA and single sign-on authentication server. It is a forward-auth companion for reverse proxies (nginx, Traefik, Caddy, Envoy, HAProxy, Skipper), authenticating against a file or LDAP backend and issuing access-control decisions to protect self-hosted applications, with an optional built-in OpenID Certified OpenID Connect 1.0 Provider. There is no commercial edition or SaaS offering; the project is entirely community-maintained.

featureList.description: First-factor authentication against a file (YAML) or LDAP backend, with Argon2id (default) or SHA512 password hashing.
No built-in social/OAuth identity provider login; Authelia is itself an identity provider, not a relying party.
Passwordless logins via Passkeys, supported since v4.39.0, in addition to multi-credential WebAuthn security keys.
No email-OTP/magic-link passwordless first factor; password reset and identity verification use emailed links, not authentication itself.
Access control supports a bypass policy for unauthenticated routing, but there is no anonymous/guest user session concept.
Only TOTP is supported for one-time password second factor; HOTP is not documented.
Legacy FIDO U2F is superseded by FIDO2/WebAuthn security key support.
FIDO2/WebAuthn hardware security keys (e.g. YubiKey), with multiple credential registration since v4.38.0.
Not documented as a built-in feature.
Duo Push mobile app second factor, via the third-party Duo API.
Not documented as a risk-based/adaptive authentication feature.
OAuth 2.0 Step-up Authentication Challenge is listed as unsupported in the OIDC support chart, though access control policies can require two_factor per route/domain.
OpenID Certified OpenID Connect 1.0 Provider.
SAML 2.0 Profile for OAuth 2.0 is listed as unsupported; Authelia does not implement a SAML IdP.
OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant for statically configured confidential clients.
Authelia is an OIDC Provider only; it does not act as a relying party federating to upstream OIDC IdPs.
LDAP authentication backend, with tested implementations for Active Directory, OpenLDAP, LLDAP, FreeIPA, and others.
Not documented; LDAP integration targets Active Directory/LDAP servers directly, not Azure AD/Entra ID over OIDC/SAML federation.
The file backend is manually edited YAML with no bulk import tool; the LDAP backend is managed externally, and no SCIM API exists (open feature request).
The file backend documents supported hash formats (Argon2id, SHA512) for manually provisioned entries; no dedicated legacy-hash migration tool is documented.
SCIM 2.0 support is an open feature request, not implemented.
Users must already exist in the file or LDAP backend; Authelia does not create accounts on first login.
Self-service password reset and WebAuthn/TOTP device registration, gated by emailed identity verification links.
Regulation (brute-force ban) temporarily bans a user/IP after repeated failed attempts; there is no persistent admin-triggered account disable in the file/LDAP backends themselves.
The file backend supports standard attributes (email, display name, groups) but no arbitrary custom user metadata schema.
No admin UI or API for searching users; management is via the backing file/LDAP store directly.

Access control rules match on user/group subjects, domains, resources, methods and networks to assign bypass/one_factor/two_factor/deny policies; this is policy-based rather than a formal role hierarchy.
No multi-organization/tenant model; each deployment is a single instance.
Standard policy (min length, character classes) or zxcvbn-based strength metering.
Access control rules can condition policies on network/subject attributes, but there is no general-purpose attribute-based policy engine beyond the built-in rule matcher.
Per-domain, per-resource-path, per-method, per-network access control rules with bypass/one_factor/two_factor/deny policies.
Forward-auth gate for reverse-proxied APIs, plus OAuth 2.0 scopes/audience for OIDC-protected APIs.
No built-in data export tooling; self-hosted operators have direct access to the backing store.
No built-in account deletion API; erasure is a manual operation on the file/LDAP/database backend.
OpenID Connect consent screen (pre-configured or interactive) per client/scope.
Self-hosted in any region; no managed hosting offering exists.
Deployable via Docker, Kubernetes, or bare-metal binary, with SQLite/MySQL/PostgreSQL storage and Redis for HA session state.
Structured logs of authentication and authorization events; retention is operator-configured.
Logs can be written to file or stdout for collection by external log shippers/SIEM; no native streaming integration.
Sensitive fields (TOTP secrets, WebAuthn keys, OIDC session data) are encrypted in the storage backend using a configured HMAC/encryption secret.
TLS for the web portal and SMTP notifier, with certificate validation.
Full key/secret management control via self-hosted deployment, including OIDC JWKS signing keys.
Regulation module bans a user after a configurable number of failed attempts within a time window, plus adaptive minimum-delay authentication timing to resist username enumeration.
Token-bucket rate limiters on authentication-sensitive endpoints, configurable per use case.
Not documented; password policy covers strength (standard rules or zxcvbn), not breach-corpus checks.
Single-instance deployment; no multi-organization branding model.
Second-factor requirements are set per access-control rule (domain/resource/network), not per organization.
Authentication happens on Authelia's own portal; no embeddable widget/SDK-driven inline login.
Built-in light/dark/auto themes and a configurable logo; full CSS/branding overrides require disabling the default Content-Security-Policy, which the docs discourage.
The portal UI is translated into numerous community-contributed languages.
No built-in analytics dashboard; structured logs can feed external tooling.
No official client SDKs; integration is via standard OAuth 2.0/OIDC libraries or the forward-auth proxy contract.
No REST management API; configuration is file-based (YAML) with environment variable/secret overrides.
Configurable per-endpoint rate limiters for authentication-sensitive routes.
No scripting/custom-code extensibility hooks; behavior is driven entirely by declarative YAML configuration.
Self-hosted on any domain, with multi-cookie-domain support for protecting multiple root domains from one instance.
authelia CLI binary and Docker/Kubernetes manifests for configuration validation and deployment; no interactive admin CLI beyond config management.
No official Authelia Terraform provider; configuration is plain YAML, which can be templated by generic Terraform file/template resources.
SQLite, MySQL/MariaDB, or PostgreSQL storage backends, plus Redis/Redis Sentinel for session/cache high availability.
Notification system modernization (webhook notifier) is an open feature request, not yet implemented.
Logo and theme are configurable; deeper HTML/CSS customization requires relaxing the built-in Content-Security-Policy.
SMTP notifier (with a filesystem notifier for testing only).
HTML and plaintext notification templates (password reset, WebAuthn/TOTP registration) are overridable per template_path.
Per-client claims_policy configuration maps custom scopes/claims onto ID tokens and userinfo responses.
No documented support for AI agent/workload identity tokens beyond standard OAuth 2.0 client_credentials.

Authelia (written in Go) can terminate TLS itself in addition to the common reverse-proxy deployment, so the underlying stack is Go's crypto/tls, which supports the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid group since Go 1.24 (Feb 2025). However, the Authelia project has published no documentation, changelog entry, or statement claiming post-quantum/hybrid TLS key-exchange support, and self-hosted deployments usually rely on external reverse proxies. Without vendor evidence, status is unknown.

No evidence found of ML-DSA/Dilithium, SLH-DSA/SPHINCS+, or FN-DSA/Falcon support for OIDC ID token or JWT signing. Targeted GitHub searches of authelia/authelia issues/discussions for quantum-related terms returned no results.
No public roadmap, blog post, whitepaper, or GitHub discussion found describing PQC migration plans or a crypto-agility/quantum-readiness statement from the Authelia project.
No public evidence found that the provider supports ML-KEM or HPKE (RFC 9180) for encrypting JWE tokens, SAML assertions, or user secrets.
No public evidence found of post-quantum or hybrid X.509 digital certificate support for mTLS client authentication or federation endpoints.
No public evidence found of NIST SP 800-208 stateful hash-based signature scheme support (LMS/HSS, XMSS).
